conflicts: AI-drafting line. Audit 'Build this first': 'For text the app wrote, the same component adds: "Drafted with AI help (Claude), October 2026. Plan: every AI line and that check are dropped; app-written text is given a named source or cut to what a source or the text shows.

AI reviewers. findings.problem: AF-LX changes Ask the Bible and the search box. It owns web/src/data/atlas.ts "langName only" and makes it return "Aramaic, written in Greek letters (scholars differ)". On main, langName is also called by web/src/ui/ask/AskSheet.tsx:244, which builds the tie reason "shares the <langName> word ...", and by web/src/ui/Palette.tsx:157 (search rows). So the change would alter visible Ask text, against decision 16 ("Ask the Bible stays as it is") and the computed task ("stays exactly as it is"). It would also change the search box, against the CLAUDE.md rule "Keep the search box as it is", which is the very reason the plan holds AF-SP. Rule 8's list of untouchable files leaves out shared helpers that Ask imports.
findings.fix: Leave langName as it is. Add a new function (for example langLabel) that only WordStudy.tsx (and the Aramaic panel, if wanted) calls. Extend rule 8 to read: "no change to the output of any function that web/src/ui/ask/* or Palette.tsx imports (atlas.ts langName, kit.tsx, depth.ts strings)". Add a gate G step that compares AskSheet's rendered tie reasons and the palette rows for 20 fixed queries before and after, and requires them to match byte for byte.

findings.problem: AF-CK's "Refuses AI-credit wording in the built data and in web/src strings" cannot be "clean on main" without touching Ask. On main, AskSheet.tsx:414 holds the founder's note, kept word for word by decision 16 ("... even AI and algorithms"). config/questions.json has Ask questions such as "Is it wrong to use AI?" (lines 7047, 9826, 14521 and others). The built ask/index.json and ask/signals.json match \bAI\b and claude. The BSB and the dictionaries name the city Ai. A loose check either fails on main or pushes a builder to edit Ask. AF-K's cite.rs rule "no AI wording in any field" needs the same care.
findings.fix: Define the refusal as a fixed list of case-sensitive credit phrases ("Drafted with", "AI help", "Claude", "AI reviewer", "AI session", "with AI", "by AI", "Not yet reviewed by a person"). Apply it only to credit-bearing strings: cite and detail fields, shelf.json, NOTICE.md, README.md, the children of SourceLine, SourceNote and Credit, and the source and credit fields of config files. Exempt by path web/src/ui/ask/*, config/questions.json, config/ask-examples.json and the built ask/ and search/ data, with decision 16 named as the reason. Never scan Bible text or entry names (Ai). Add a test that the founder's note on AskSheet.tsx:414 passes.

findings.problem: Several modules put writers' views into surfaces the commentary notice deliberately leaves open, so commentary would reach readers without the two-page notice. The founder made that notice binding (decision 1: "the first time viewers look at commentary, any commentary"). NOTICE-SPEC.md (notice scratch folder, lines 36 to 46 and decision 3) keeps open the Aramaic notes, parallels, roads and paths, and the alphabet poems, because today they hold only facts about the text. The plan then adds commentary to them: AF-AR writes "Keil holds that ..." at Simple; AF-PA's kind notes quote a shelf work such as the Tyndale dictionary word for word, or name the writers who hold a view; AF-WP credits the poem notes to cite-list writers; and AF-X's A11 captions "name the writer whose reading it is, with a fetched quote". AF-AR, AF-PA and AF-X do not wait for commentary-notice.
findings.fix: AF-AR, AF-PA and AF-X wait for commentary-notice. Any line that reports a writer's view or quotes a commentary or dictionary is shown through the notice's gate (its commentaryNoticeDone and showCommentaryNotice API), or kept behind a surface already gated. Otherwise the module cuts the sentence to what the text shows, which also fits decision 15. Add each new gated spot to the notice's coverage check, and add a browser check per module that no writer's view shows before the notice is finished.

findings.problem: AF-SH and WD will each create a card for the same works. AF-SH adds cards for every Layers-cited work ("Gill, Barnes (and Murphy and Pusey), JFB, Clarke ...") and makes the build refuse a cited work with no card. WD adds a writers-group card for each of its works (VOICES-BUILD-SPEC 3.5: JFB, Keil and Delitzsch, Barnes on the New Testament, Henry's complete commentary, Calvin, Luther). Whichever lands second adds a second card for the same work, or an id collision (jfb, keil-delitzsch, barnes). Readers would see two cards for one work, with their citation counts split.
findings.fix: Rule: one card per work, keyed by the cite id in config/layer-sources.json. If AF-SH lands first, it creates the card with the Layers count, and WD's VI extends that card (datasets, licenseNote, copy) instead of adding one. If WD's card exists, AF-SH attaches the Layers count to it. Write this into AF-SH's Does and send it to WD's integrator as a fragment rule, listing the overlapping ids.

findings.problem: Some ownership is not exclusive and the order does not say so. build.rs is edited by AF-LX (about line 466), AF-DT (meta, about 525 to 545), AF-WR (possibly a line) and WD V1 (line 412). Whether these limits still bind outside parallel extra work is an open founder decision"), and section 7 does not list this. Add "not while WD's V12 is open" to AF-LE in section 3 and in row 19 of the order.

findings.problem: Gate G's U+2014 scan of "the built data" will hit quoted sources. The built bsb.txt has 1,314 lines with em dashes, and the hard-verses and notes extras have them too. Modules that quote sources word for word (AF-PA's kind notes, AF-ER's Irenaeus, AF-CW's Wesley prefaces, AF-LE's stored quotes) can add em dashes legitimately, because decision 4 says to cite "exactly how the commentary shows". A builder chasing "0 new hits" might change a quotation.
findings.fix: Scope the em dash check to strings the app writes (UI strings, credits, notes the app wrote, config prose), and exempt quotations and source text by field, with decision 4 named as the reason.

findings.problem: AF-AR writes writers' names into note text ("Keil holds that ..."), and its verify check requires each interpretive sentence to name a writer. CLAUDE.md says "Sources go in the evidence field, never in a note's text". Section 7 does not raise this as a conflict.
findings.fix: Keep the note text clean. Add a structured by field per sentence or per note in config/aramaic.json, and have the panel render "Keil holds that" from it. Or list this in section 7 as a conflict for the founder.

findings.problem: AF-K builds the citation shape before TC's CREDITS-SPEC.md exists. TC's design phase has not run, and its scratch credits folder has no spec yet. The plan accepts a rename "in one commit when TC merges", but by then AF-Q, AF-SY, AF-PA and AF-AR will have written the audit's field names into config/aramaic.json detail arrays and config/parallels.json sources, files AF-K does not own. That leaves two shapes, or a rename across merged modules' data.
findings.fix: Have AF-K wait only for TC's Design phase output (CREDITS-SPEC.md, not TC's merge), which is cheap and soon, so that one shape is fixed before any config adopts it. Or freeze the audit's names and send them to TC as its input.

findings.problem: Some checks have no owned file. AF-CW's new verify check ("every shown Catena name has a who line") needs code in extra_voices/catena.rs or extra_voices.rs, which AF-CW does not own (catena.rs passes to AF-FL). AF-PA's check that "every quotation in a kind note is found word for word" needs the kind notes, which live in web/src/ui/extras/parallels/notes.tsx, where the Rust build cannot read them.
findings.fix: Give AF-CW extra_voices/catena.rs (passing it to AF-FL afterwards), or move the who-line check into AF-FL. Have AF-PA move the kind notes into config/parallels.json (which it owns), so extra_parallels.rs can check them against the pinned text.

findings.problem: Some deletions can leave a selection empty, against decision 12. AF-PA drops any added passage without a source, which can leave a parallel set of one passage. AF-HP drops Catholic Answers pages, which can leave a hard passage with no link: verify's "at least one link" rule would fail, and the plan gives no path forward. AF-WP and AF-AR may cut a note or sentence to nothing.
findings.fix: State the rule in each module: when a cut leaves a set with fewer than two passages, a passage with no link, or an empty note, the line or chip is removed with it (or a sourced replacement is found), and a browser check opens each affected verse.

findings.problem: AF-LR's label overclaims what was read. It labels a cite "Read at <site> on <date>" when the page loaded and its heading was found, but the cite's point was not re-read. TC's own research (credits/dates.md line 26) says: "Never show a page's retrieval date on a cite whose own point was not re-read that day." Decision 10 asks for the "truly retrieved timestamp".
findings.fix: Use "page retrieved <date>" for a fetch that only found the heading. Keep "read on <date>" for cites whose stored quote was found on the fetched page, which AF-LR's evidence file already records. Follow TC's spec if it settles the words.

findings.problem: Reader-facing PR links lead readers to AI credit. AF-ER's footer cites "(PR #11)", and AF-SH's "Compiled for this app" cards list "its PRs". Those GitHub pages carry Claude-Session trailers, Co-Authored-By Claude lines and "Generated with Claude Code". The founder said: "No crediting of AI" anywhere.
findings.fix: In reader text, name the founder's choices by date ("the founder's choices of 11 October 2026") and leave PR numbers to docs/HANDOFF.md and the evidence files. AF-SH's cards say what each compilation rests on and its rules, without PR links.

findings.problem: The plan gives some work to two modules, and leaves some exemptions and evidence rules unsaid. README.md 195 is assigned to both AF-X ("Hands the integrator ... README.md 195") and AF-SH (B1). AF-SH repeats the TAHOT, TBESH and TBESG card work that AF-BT and AF-LX already hand over. AF-WR's new config/abbott-smith-abbreviations.json names avoid-listed works (Thayer, BDB, ICC, Meyer), but AF-CK does not exempt it by name. A check "over every config file that names a writer" (the audit's D1) would refuse it. AF-X's evidence would store OpenBible.info's own page text as a quote, where rule 6 asks for a pointer for copyrighted pages and CLAUDE.md keeps OpenBible.info material out of the repository.
findings.fix: Give README 195 to AF-X only. AF-SH applies AF-BT's and AF-LX's card fragments instead of redoing the catalogue checks. AF-CK lists the abbreviations table as exempt, with question 5's reason ("names inside a quoted work's own words"). AF-X's evidence records OpenBible.info's page as URL, time and SHA-256 with a pointer, not the quote.
